subject: Scaling request and commercial options for 32-GPU reserved pool (RetrieverX)
messages:
From: Aaliyah Khan <aaliyah.k@retrieverx.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@retrieverx.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Scaling request: dedicated GPU expansion at renewal

Hi Irene / Ben,

Hope youre well. Were heading into renewal for our Dedicated pool on Dec 1 and want to discuss moving from our current 16-GPU reserved pool to 32 GPUs. Over the last quarter our production RAG workload has doubled and were already seeing throttling during peak windows.

High-level asks from our side:
- Commercials for a 12-month reserved commitment at 32 GPUs (whats the per-hour reserved rate vs. our current rate?)
- A staged upgrade path (we may want to step 16 -> 24 -> 32 over 2–3 months) and how that impacts pricing
- Throughput guarantees for the pool (we need predictable tail throughput for batch generation jobs and low-latency inference during spikes)
- Procurement timeline and any required SOW or SOC2 artifacts

Can you send options and a recommended path this week? Were aiming to sign by Nov 20 so legal/procurement can process the PO before Dec 1.

Thanks,
Aaliyah
Aaliyah Khan
Head of Platform Engineering
RetrieverX

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Scaling request: dedicated GPU expansion at renewal

Thanks Aaliyah — we can absolutely support a path to 32 GPUs. Ill propose two commercial options below and flag the technical throughput guarantees so everyone knows what to expect operationally. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through.

Option A — Immediate 32-GPU commit (preferred for unit economics)
- Term: 12 months starting Dec 1
- Capacity: 32x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs
- Reserved rate (blended): $2.75 / GPU-hour
- One-time onboarding & validation: $7,500 (includes runbook review + SOC2 evidence handoff)
- SLA: 99.9% pool availability; throughput commitment: baseline sustained aggregate throughput of 250k tokens/min with 5% tolerance on monthly windows; burst capacity available up to 350k tokens/min with graceful degradation

Option B — Staged ramp (16 -> 24 -> 32)
- Term: 12 months starting Dec 1
- Month 1–2: 16 GPUs reserved; Month 3–12: 32 GPUs reserved (automated step-up on schedule)
- Blended reserved rate: $2.95 / GPU-hour (higher due to staging)
- One-time onboarding: $5,000 (fewer validation hours initially; full validation after final step-up)
- SLA: 99.8% pool availability; throughput commitment scaled to actual active capacity (well guarantee proportional throughput during step months with a final baseline equivalent to Option A once at 32 GPUs)

Notes on guarantees and operational expectations:
- Throughput guarantees are tied to traffic profile we observed in your perf tests. If youre running heavy long-context workloads well need a short baseline test (we can run a 2-hour validation window before the final step-up).
- Warm-up for cold KV/cache populations: burst windows may see 20–40s higher latency until caches populate; we include warm-warmup mitigations in the runbook.
- We can add a 30% burst buffer for a short-term add-on (pay-as-you-burst) if RetrieverX expects unpredictable spikes during holiday promotions.

Next steps: Ill draft a short SOW and price sheet and share — would love a 30-minute sync on Monday (Nov 9) to align on staging preference and procurement needs.

Best,
Irene Choi

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Scaling request: dedicated GPU expansion at renewal — Commercial + technical appendix

Aaliyah / team — following our Monday sync Ive attached the commercial appendix and a short technical runbook excerpt (attachments: SOW_v3.pdf, throughput_runbook.xlsx). Summarizing agreed points and clarifications based on legal/procurement requests: 

1) Staged ramp schedule (confirmed)
- Dec 1–Jan 31: 16 GPUs reserved (monthly billable)
- Feb 1–Feb 28: 24 GPUs reserved
- Mar 1 onward: 32 GPUs reserved for remainder of term (through Nov 30, 2027)

2) Billing impact
- We will bill the actual reserved capacity per month (you will see line items for 16/24/32 GPU-hours based on calendar month).

3) Throughput guarantee (absolute form requested by Legal)
- Final state (from Mar 1): guaranteed aggregate baseline throughput of 250,000 tokens/min at p95 for the 32-GPU pool; burst envelope up to 350,000 tokens/min for windows up to 60 minutes (subject to a 10-minute warm-up).
- During staged months we commit to a proportional baseline: 125,000 tokens/min p95 in Dec/Jan (16 GPUs), 187,500 tokens/min p95 in Feb (24 GPUs).
- Penalty: 3 days of credit (pro-rated) for any month where p95 throughput falls below 90% of the committed baseline after agreed validation tests (we included measurement methodology in throughput_runbook.xlsx).

4) Pricing (finalized options)
- Staged (Option B) — Blended reserved rate: $2.95 / GPU-hour (12-month term). One-time onboarding: $5,000.
- Immediate (Option A) — Full 32 commit: $2.75 / GPU-hour. One-time onboarding: $7,500.
- Note: all rates exclude applicable taxes. We can provide a true-up calculator for forecasting monthly charges.

5) Security / compliance deliverables
- Well provide SOC2 report, network architecture diagram, and the SAML SSO metadata. Full package attached.

6) Next steps
- RetrieverX to confirm staged vs immediate by EOD Nov 15 so Legal can prepare the PO/Amendment.
- If staged: we will plan the Feb 1 automatic increase; Procurement should confirm a PO that covers provisional billing for Feb and Mar to avoid provisioning lag.

Ive included Aditya for the runbook/ops handoff — Aditya will schedule the 2-hour validation window before the Mar 1 final step-up.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
